meaning.en: Nothing is truly secret; used both to say 'only the two of us know' and to warn that wrongdoing will be known.
meaning.zh: 天地都知道，形容事情隐秘；也用来表示“做了坏事迟早会被发现”。

examples.zh: 这事天知地知，你知我知，绝不会有第三个人知道。
examples.en: This is between heaven, earth, you and me; no third person will ever know.

examples.zh: 他以为天知地知，没想到监控拍得一清二楚。
examples.en: He thought nobody would ever know, but the cameras caught everything.

examples.zh: 天知地知，我问心无愧。
examples.en: Heaven and earth are my witnesses; my conscience is clear.

story.en: Yang Zhen refused a bribe offered at night 'because no one will know', replying: 'Heaven knows, the spirits know, I know and you know. How can you say no one knows?' (天知，神知，我知，子知).
story.zh: 杨震拒收夜晚送来的贿金，说：“天知，神知，我知，子知。何谓无知者！”

usage.en: Usually in the fuller form 天知，地知，你知，我知. Can be sincere (clear conscience) or wry (a secret deal).
usage.zh: 常见全句“天知地知，你知我知”；可表问心无愧，也可用于私下交易的口吻。

meaning.en: To show reluctance or embarrassment on one's face when asked to do something.
meaning.zh: 脸上露出为难的神情。

examples.zh: 听说要加班，他面有难色。
examples.en: On hearing there would be overtime, he looked reluctant.

examples.zh: 我提出借钱时，朋友面有难色。
examples.en: When I asked to borrow money, my friend looked uncomfortable.

examples.zh: 老板让她出差，她面有难色，却没有拒绝。
examples.en: The boss told her to travel; she looked unwilling but did not refuse.

usage.en: Predicate; mild and polite, describing hesitation shown on the face.
usage.zh: 作谓语，语气委婉，描写神色上的为难。

meaning.en: A bitter enemy or rival; people who are always at odds.
meaning.zh: 仇敌；互相对立、总是作对的人。

examples.zh: 这两家是多年的冤家对头。
examples.en: The two families have been sworn enemies for years.

examples.zh: 没想到我们竟成了冤家对头。
examples.en: I never expected us to become bitter rivals.

examples.zh: 他们俩就是一对冤家对头，见面就吵。
examples.en: Those two are arch-enemies and quarrel the moment they meet.

usage.en: Can be serious (real enmity) or teasing (squabbling pairs, even lovers). 冤家 is read yuān jiā (jia sometimes soft).
usage.zh: 可指真正的仇人，也可戏称爱吵架的一对；“冤家”口语中“家”可轻读。

meaning.en: To show no respect for age or seniority; to behave without proper manners between elders and juniors.
meaning.zh: 不分长幼尊卑，对长辈或上级缺乏礼貌。

equivalents: show no respect for one's elders

examples.zh: 你怎么跟爷爷说话呢，没大没小的！
examples.en: How can you talk to Grandpa like that? Have some respect!

examples.zh: 这孩子被惯坏了，没大没小。
examples.en: The child is spoiled and has no respect for elders.

examples.zh: 我们办公室气氛轻松，同事之间没大没小地开玩笑。
examples.en: The atmosphere in our office is relaxed and colleagues joke without regard to rank.

usage.en: Usually a scolding for a child or a young person, but can be affectionate banter. 没 is méi.
usage.zh: 多用于责备小辈，也可作亲昵的玩笑。

natural: a hundred and none of them useful

meaning.en: Completely useless; good for nothing.
meaning.zh: 什么用处也没有，毫无用处。

examples.zh: 他自嘲说，百无一用是书生。
examples.en: He joked that scholars are good for nothing.

examples.zh: 这堆旧设备早已百无一用。
examples.en: The pile of old equipment is utterly useless now.

examples.zh: 别觉得自己百无一用，你只是还没找到擅长的事。
examples.en: Don't think you're useless; you just haven't found what you're good at.

usage.en: Often from the line 百无一用是书生 ('a scholar is good for nothing'), said in self-mockery. Strongly negative about others.
usage.zh: 常见于“百无一用是书生”的自嘲，用于他人则贬义很重。

natural: of no bearing on the main point

meaning.en: Irrelevant to the main point; not important.
meaning.zh: 与主要意思、主要问题没有关系，无关紧要。

examples.zh: 这些细节无关宏旨，可以略去。
examples.en: These details are beside the point and can be left out.

examples.zh: 无关宏旨的争论，不必再继续。
examples.en: There's no need to continue an argument that does not matter.

examples.zh: 他纠结于一些无关宏旨的小事。
examples.en: He fusses about trivial matters that make no difference.

usage.en: Formal; used in judging what to leave out or argue about. Often misspelled 无关紧旨; the standard form is 宏旨.
usage.zh: 较庄重，用于判断取舍；注意是“宏旨”。

meaning.en: Good-looking, with red lips and white teeth; describes a handsome, healthy-looking child or youth.
meaning.zh: 嘴唇红润，牙齿洁白，形容容貌俊美，多指少年或儿童。

examples.zh: 这个唇红齿白的小男孩特别惹人喜爱。
examples.en: The rosy-lipped little boy was very lovable.

examples.zh: 画中的少年唇红齿白，眉清目秀。
examples.en: The youth in the painting is fresh-faced and delicately featured.

examples.zh: 他唇红齿白，像个书生。
examples.en: He looks fresh-faced and handsome, like a young scholar.

usage.en: Descriptive and admiring; usually of young people, boys more often than women.
usage.zh: 描写容貌，含赞美，多用于少年、儿童。

natural: creatures grieve for their own kind

meaning.en: To feel sorrow when one of one's own kind meets misfortune; sympathy for fellow sufferers.
meaning.zh: 动物为同类的死亡或不幸而悲伤，比喻人因同伙的不幸而感到悲伤。

equivalents: feel for one of one's own kind

examples.zh: 同行遭此打击，大家物伤其类，都很难过。
examples.en: The whole trade was saddened by the blow to a fellow practitioner.

examples.zh: 看到邻村遭灾，村民们物伤其类。
examples.en: Seeing the neighbouring village struck by disaster, the villagers felt for them as their own.

examples.zh: 他对那位落魄的老同行物伤其类。
examples.en: He felt keenly for the old colleague who had fallen on hard times.

usage.en: Often in the pair 兔死狐悲，物伤其类. May suggest self-interested worry (it could happen to me) as well as pure sympathy.
usage.zh: 常与“兔死狐悲”并用；既可表同情，也暗含兔死狐悲、担心自身的意味。

natural: a full head and fat bowels

meaning.en: Fat and bloated from a life of ease; describes a gluttonous, idle, well-fed rich person.
meaning.zh: 形容不劳而获、吃得又胖又蠢的剥削者或富人。

examples.zh: 他是个脑满肠肥的大老板。
examples.en: He is a fat, self-indulgent big boss.

examples.zh: 那些脑满肠肥的官员只顾吃喝享乐。
examples.en: Those bloated officials care only for eating, drinking and pleasure.

examples.zh: 漫画里脑满肠肥的形象代表了贪婪。
examples.en: The bloated figure in the cartoon stands for greed.

usage.en: Contemptuous, often political; describes parasitic wealthy people or officials. Do not use it of someone who is merely plump.
usage.zh: 带蔑视，多用于不劳而获的富人、官员；不要用于单纯的胖。

natural: a petty person gets his way

meaning.en: A mean or petty person who gains power or success and becomes insufferably arrogant.
meaning.zh: 品行不端的人一旦得势，就得意忘形、嚣张起来。

equivalents: a petty person flushed with success

examples.zh: 他刚升职就对同事颐指气使，真是小人得志。
examples.en: Just promoted, he orders colleagues about; a typical case of a petty person on top.

examples.zh: 别看他现在小人得志，早晚要栽跟头。
examples.en: Never mind his swagger now; he'll fall flat sooner or later.

examples.zh: 小人得志的嘴脸，让人看了就反感。
examples.en: The smug look of the upstart makes one's stomach turn.

usage.en: Strongly negative; a judgement of character, not just of luck. Often 小人得志便猖狂 ('a petty man in power turns arrogant').
usage.zh: 贬义很强，是对品性的评判；常说“小人得志便猖狂”。

literal: not · can · stand on tiptoe · reach

meaning.en: Beyond reach; impossible to equal or match.
meaning.zh: 没法赶上或达到，形容水平高得无法匹敌。

examples.zh: 他的技艺已到了常人不可企及的境界。
examples.en: His craft has reached a level that ordinary people cannot match.

examples.zh: 这样的成就在当时是不可企及的。
examples.en: Such an achievement was out of reach at the time.

examples.zh: 她对我来说，似乎遥不可及，不可企及。
examples.en: To me she seems far away, beyond anyone's reach.

usage.en: Often attributive (不可企及的高度) or after 是. 企 means to stand on tiptoe; do not confuse with 企业 (qǐ yè).
usage.zh: 常作定语（不可企及的高度）或谓语；“企”指踮起脚。

meaning.en: To be forgotten and left unknown; fame or achievements lost to history.
meaning.zh: 被埋没，不为人知。

examples.zh: 许多优秀的民间艺人湮没无闻。
examples.en: Many fine folk artists have vanished into obscurity.

examples.zh: 他的发明曾湮没无闻，多年后才被重视。
examples.en: His invention languished unnoticed and was valued only years later.

examples.zh: 这座古城湮没无闻已久，近年才被发掘。
examples.en: The ancient city lay forgotten for ages and was excavated only in recent years.

usage.en: Literary; implies loss or waste of talent or heritage. 湮 is yān. Close to 默默无闻 but stresses being buried.
usage.zh: 书面语，含人才或遗产被埋没的惋惜；与“默默无闻”相近，但强调被埋没。

meaning.en: Any random person or thing; anybody at all (usually dismissive).
meaning.zh: 随便什么人或东西，泛指无足轻重的人。

examples.zh: 这个职位可不是阿猫阿狗都能做的。
examples.en: This post is not for just anybody.

examples.zh: 我不是阿猫阿狗，不会随便见客。
examples.en: I'm not just anybody; I don't see visitors at random.

examples.zh: 别什么阿猫阿狗的话都信。
examples.en: Don't believe every random person's word.

usage.en: Casual, dismissive; used to stress that something is exclusive. Do not use it face to face with respect.
usage.zh: 口语，含轻视，常用来强调“不是随便什么人都行”；当面使用不礼貌。

meaning.en: Looking worn, pale and thin, from illness, grief or exhaustion.
meaning.zh: 面容瘦弱、神色疲惫，多因病痛、忧愁或劳累。

examples.zh: 连日守在病床前，她已形容憔悴。
examples.en: After days at the bedside, she looked drawn and worn out.

examples.zh: 他失业半年，形容憔悴，让人心疼。
examples.en: Unemployed for half a year, he looked haggard and it pained us to see.

examples.zh: 见到形容憔悴的老友，我心里一酸。
examples.en: Seeing my old friend look so haggard, my heart ached.

usage.en: Predicate; 形容 here is a noun (looks, appearance), not 'to describe'. 悴 is cuì. Compare 形容枯槁.
usage.zh: 作谓语；“形容”此处指面貌，不是“描述”；“悴”读cuì；与“形容枯槁”相近。

pinyin: bǐ shàng bù zú, bǐ xià yǒu yú
literal: compared · up · not · enough, compared · down · has · extra
natural: not as good as those above, better than those below

meaning.en: Not as good as the best but better than the worst; an average or acceptable position, often a self-consoling remark.
meaning.zh: 比不上最好的，但比差的强，指处在中等水平，常用来自我安慰。

equivalents: not the best, not the worst
better than some, worse than others

examples.zh: 我们家的收入比上不足，比下有余。
examples.en: Our family income is not the best, but better than many.

examples.zh: 他的成绩比上不足，比下有余，不算差。
examples.en: His grades are not top, but better than the lowest; not bad.

examples.zh: 比上不足，比下有余，知足常乐吧。
examples.en: Not the best, but better than some; be content and happy.

usage.en: Either half can stand alone. Often used to console oneself, or as a modest summary of one's situation.
usage.zh: 两半句可单用；常用于自我安慰或谦虚地概括自己的处境。

natural: a thousand li of fertile plain

meaning.en: A vast expanse of rich, fertile land.
meaning.zh: 肥沃的土地一望无际。

examples.zh: 这片沃野千里的平原是国家的粮仓。
examples.en: This vast fertile plain is the nation's granary.

examples.zh: 黑土地上沃野千里，一眼望不到边。
examples.en: On the black soil the fertile fields stretch as far as the eye can see.

examples.zh: 古人称四川盆地为沃野千里的天府之国。
examples.en: The ancients called the Sichuan Basin a land of plenty with fertile fields for a thousand li.

usage.en: Literary praise of land. 沃 is wò (fertile). 千里 is not literal.
usage.zh: 书面赞语，形容土地；“沃”读wò；“千里”不是实指。

natural: the ink is not yet dry

meaning.en: Recently written; something has just been agreed or put in writing, and already changes or is broken.
meaning.zh: 字迹还没有干，比喻刚写好不久，多含“承诺、协议刚签就变”的讽意。

examples.zh: 协议的墨迹未干，对方就违约了。
examples.en: The ink on the agreement was hardly dry before the other side broke it.

examples.zh: 他的毕业证书墨迹未干，就已经开始创业。
examples.en: The ink on his diploma was barely dry when he started a business.

examples.zh: 条约墨迹未干，战火又起。
examples.en: The ink of the treaty was hardly dry before fighting broke out again.

usage.en: Usually in the pattern 'X's ink was not yet dry, and…', to highlight how quickly something changed. Compare English 'the ink is barely dry'.
usage.zh: 常用在“……墨迹未干，就……”的句式中，突出变化之快；与英语“the ink is barely dry”相近。

meaning.en: To get to the point and keep it brief.
meaning.zh: 把要说的话简短地说，不啰嗦。

equivalents: to cut a long story short

examples.zh: 时间不多，我长话短说。
examples.en: We're short of time, so I'll make it brief.

examples.zh: 长话短说，这件事大家都同意了。
examples.en: To cut a long story short, everyone agreed.

examples.zh: 你就长话短说吧，我马上要开会。
examples.en: Keep it short, please; I have a meeting soon.

usage.en: Often used as an opener or interruption. Compare the English 'to cut a long story short'.
usage.zh: 常作开场白或打断对方的话；相当于英语的“to cut a long story short”。

natural: love the people like one's children

meaning.en: To treat the people with a parent's care, as a good official or ruler does.
meaning.zh: 像爱自己的孩子一样爱护百姓，多形容清官、好官。

equivalents: love one's people as one's own children

examples.zh: 他当县令时爱民如子，深受百姓拥戴。
examples.en: As county magistrate he cared for the people as his own children and was loved by them.

examples.zh: 这位爱民如子的市长赢得了市民的尊敬。
examples.en: The mayor, who cared for citizens like family, won their respect.

examples.zh: 为官一任，应当爱民如子。
examples.en: An official ought to treat the people as his own children.

usage.en: Praise of officials and rulers; slightly traditional, paternalistic tone.
usage.zh: 赞扬官员、君主；带传统的“父母官”色彩。

natural: shut the door and reflect on one's faults

meaning.en: To stay by oneself and reflect on one's mistakes.
meaning.zh: 关起门来，独自反省自己的过错。

equivalents: reflect on one's faults in private

examples.zh: 犯错之后，他闭门思过了一个星期。
examples.en: After his mistake he spent a week reflecting on it in seclusion.

examples.zh: 老师让他回家闭门思过。
examples.en: The teacher told him to go home and think about what he'd done.

examples.zh: 公司要求涉事部门闭门思过，整改到位。
examples.en: The company ordered the department involved to reflect and put things right.

usage.en: Can be a self-imposed act or a punishment ('go to your room and think'). Often news about officials made to reflect.
usage.zh: 可指自觉反省，也可指受罚反省（类似“回房反省”）。

meaning.en: Having limitless supernatural power; also used jokingly of someone who seems able to do anything.
meaning.zh: 神通无比，法术无穷无尽；也戏指某人本事极大。

examples.zh: 孙悟空法力无边，却逃不出如来佛的手掌。
examples.en: Sun Wukong has boundless powers, yet cannot escape the Buddha's palm.

examples.zh: 别以为他法力无边，什么事都能摆平。
examples.en: Don't think he's all-powerful and can fix anything.

examples.zh: 传说这位仙人法力无边，能呼风唤雨。
examples.en: Legend says the immortal had limitless magic and could summon wind and rain.

usage.en: Mostly in myths, novels and games; jokingly of someone resourceful. Buddhist flavour (法力 = power of the Dharma).
usage.zh: 多用于神话、小说、游戏；也戏称神通广大的人，带佛教色彩。

meaning.en: With hair and beard all white, a sign of old age.
meaning.zh: 胡须和头发全都白了，形容年纪很大。

examples.zh: 那位须发皆白的老人是村里最年长的人。
examples.en: The white-bearded old man is the oldest in the village.

examples.zh: 几年不见，他已须发皆白。
examples.en: After a few years apart, his hair and beard have turned completely white.

examples.zh: 须发皆白的老将军依然精神矍铄。
examples.en: The white-haired old general was still hale and hearty.

usage.en: Descriptive, usually respectful, of the elderly (often men). 发 here is fà (hair).
usage.zh: 描写老年人，多用于男性，含敬意；“发”读fà。

meaning.en: Even the dragon's nine sons are all different; used to say that children of one family differ in character and ability.
meaning.zh: 传说龙生九子，各不相同，比喻同胞兄弟品性、才能各异。

equivalents: children of one family are all different

examples.zh: 龙生九子，各有不同，兄弟俩性格差别很大。
examples.en: The dragon has nine sons, each different; the two brothers are very unlike.

examples.zh: 龙生九子，一母同胞也未必一样。
examples.en: As the saying goes, a dragon's nine sons are all different; siblings may not be alike.

examples.zh: 民间传说龙生九子，其中有囚牛、睚眦等。
examples.en: Folklore says the dragon has nine sons, among them Qiuniu and Yazi.

usage.en: Usually in 龙生九子，各有所好 / 各不相同. The nine sons are a Ming-era folk tradition; names vary by source.
usage.zh: 常说“龙生九子，各不相同”；九子之说见于明代民间传说，名称因书而异。

synonyms: 一母生九子，连母十个样

meaning.en: To gossip about others and pass judgement on their affairs.
meaning.zh: 背后议论别人的是非好坏。

examples.zh: 不要在背后说长道短。
examples.en: Don't gossip behind people's backs.

examples.zh: 邻居们爱对别人家的事说长道短。
examples.en: The neighbours love to gossip about other families' business.

examples.zh: 她最讨厌被人说长道短。
examples.en: She hates being talked about.

usage.en: Negative, casual; close to 说三道四 and 评头论足, but usually of gossip about people.
usage.zh: 贬义，口语；与“说三道四”“评头论足”相近。

natural: a beauty without equal in her age

meaning.en: A woman of beauty unrivalled in her time.
meaning.zh: 当代独一无二的美人。

examples.zh: 传说西施是绝代佳人。
examples.en: Legend has it that Xi Shi was a peerless beauty.

examples.zh: 小说中的绝代佳人最后都命运多舛。
examples.en: The peerless beauties in the novels all end up with an unhappy fate.

examples.zh: 她虽不是绝代佳人，却气质出众。
examples.en: Though not a peerless beauty, she has an outstanding air.

usage.en: Literary; of women only. Sometimes used lightly or ironically in modern speech. Compare 倾国倾城.
usage.zh: 书面语，只用于女性，现代偶尔戏用；与“倾国倾城”相近。
